newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NSW AUSTRALIA WHEAT GROWERS HIT EXPORT SPLIT IDEA.
newsitem.headline: NSW AUSTRALIA WHEAT GROWERS HIT EXPORT SPLIT IDEA.

text.p: The New South Wales Farmers Association said on Tuesday the government should dismiss calls by the Western Australian Farmers Federation (WAFF) for a separate 'single desk' for the export of west coast wheat.
"Two 'single desks' is a nonsense," Xavier Martin, chairman of the NSW Farmers' Association grains committee, said in a statement.
Martin said the Australian Wheat Board (AWB), which has a monopoly on the export of Australian wheat, had an internationally renowned record in grain marketing because of its 'single desk' powers.

Earlier this year the U.S. States Department of Agriculture reported a statement by U.S. wheat traders that the single desk approach had helped Australia move into new markets and operate possibly the world's most efficient export service, Martin said.

Western Australian calls for the AWB's single desk to be split in two, with one for west coast wheat and one for the rest of Australia, have been advanced as part of a debate in Australia's grains industry about conditions which attach to shares to be issued in a privatised AWB.
